static data member|static member variabl: A member variable declared `static`: one copy per class, shared between all instances, with static storage for the life of the program; the keyword goes on the declaration in the class, and the member is defined once outside (`int X::n = 1;`). See [Static data members: one copy per class](#/comp3522-w7/static-data-members).
static member function: A member function declared `static`: it can only access static data and call static member functions, has no `*this` pointer, and cannot be virtual or const; call it as `Class::function()` without an object. See [Static member functions and the class you never instantiate](#/comp3522-w7/static-member-functions).
copy elision|copy omission: A compiler optimization that avoids unnecessary copying of objects; since C++17 it is guaranteed when an object is initialized from a prvalue of the same type. See [Copy elision and return value optimization](#/comp3522-w7/copy-elision-rvo).
return value optimization|RVO: The subset of copy elision that avoids copying objects returned from a function: the object made on the `return` statement (`return Number(num);`) is constructed straight into the caller's variable. See [Copy elision and return value optimization](#/comp3522-w7/copy-elision-rvo).
named return value optimization|NRVO: Removing the temporaries by directly initializing the caller's variable even when the returned object is named (`Number tempN(num); return tempN;`); still optional in C++17, and never applied to a function parameter. See [Copy elision and return value optimization](#/comp3522-w7/copy-elision-rvo).
prvalue: A pure rvalue, an expression such as `Number(2)` or a call returning by value that makes a new object rather than naming one; it is the thing C++17's guaranteed copy elision applies to. See [Copy elision and return value optimization](#/comp3522-w7/copy-elision-rvo).
right-left rule|right left rule: A way to read a declaration: start at the name, go right until `)`, go left until `(`, exit the parentheses and go right until `)` or `;`, then go left of where you exited until `(` or the end, repeating as needed. See [The right-left rule for reading declarations](#/comp3522-w7/right-left-rule).
declarator: The part of a declaration that names the thing and wraps it in `*`, `&`, `[]` and `()` (in `int (**var[])();` it is `(**var[])()`); the right-left rule reads it outward from the name. See [The right-left rule for reading declarations](#/comp3522-w7/right-left-rule).
virtual base class|virtual inheritance: A base inherited with `virtual` (`class B : virtual public A`), so B and C refer to a common A object that is part of the most derived class, giving a true diamond with only one A. See [Review: the three meanings of virtual](#/comp3522-w7/review-virtual).
most derived class: The class of the object actually being created (D in the diamond); with virtual inheritance it is responsible for calling the virtual base's (A's) constructor during its own construction. See [Review: the three meanings of virtual](#/comp3522-w7/review-virtual).
friend function: A non-member function that has access to the private and protected members of the class that declares it as a friend; it is not a member even though it is declared in the class, so its definition is never scoped with `MyClass::`. See [Review: kinds of functions, and the copy constructor](#/comp3522-w7/review-functions-copy-ctor).
shallow copy: What the built-in copy constructor makes: it copies the address a pointer member holds, so both objects point at the same dynamic memory. See [Review: kinds of functions, and the copy constructor](#/comp3522-w7/review-functions-copy-ctor).
deep copy: A copy constructor that allocates new dynamic memory and copies the value from the other object's pointer (`ptr(new int(*other.ptr))`), so each object has its own copy. See [Review: kinds of functions, and the copy constructor](#/comp3522-w7/review-functions-copy-ctor).
